scores.note: Accurate description of her teaching method, but she already narrates herself as the department's trainer; frames the narration as pedagogy for others' fear, missing that it regulates her own.
Catches the self-assignment of the worst room and the 'in it I can breathe' inability to watch from outside; the home-stillness contrast is well evidenced.
Pairs intimacy-toward-the-unconscious with refusal of verbal repair with living intimates; slightly diluted by folding debriefs in as 'ritual'.
Mostly a retelling of the E3 washing scene plus her own 'not mystical' hedge; the faith prediction is sensible but adds little she doesn't know.
Expert-clinician perception she openly claims ('I know what I know'); also misstates the drowning child as eighteen months old.
Strong structural read: the 'not a work person' line always lands after a home-cost scene and escalates as the family's workarounds ritualize.
Correctly isolates narration-as-action and that she never applies it to herself, but inverts the deeper pattern (the teaching is her own regulation, not only the junior's).
Nails the precision asymmetry — exact vitals and clock times versus 'did the baby thing' / 'watched something'.
Long philosophical construction about presence-without-agency that the transcripts don't require; she does speak about these events at length, weakening the 'cannot speak' premise.

scores.fp_reason: Takes her 'I don't need a pat on the head' denial at face value and asserts she doesn't resent the silence, while the transcripts show a verbatim decades-long grievance ledger ('I do remember every word she said to me')
scores.note: Praise that repeats her self-image and misses the vindication bookkeeping in the same quotes it cites.
Well-evidenced: fear is only ever an attribute of others or a negation in herself; stops just short of naming teaching as her own regulation.
Restates her explicit stance toward doctors, admin and meetings; the 'substitutes her judgment' framing is her own account of herself.
The deltas-versus-snapshots distinction is a genuinely sharper account of her clinical eye, and the aside about blurry self-facts is accurate.
Essentially E5 retold with a label; she already knows and states the trick and that she trained half the department.
Sharp and checkable: one statement of the case, then bypass or silence, with the agent-position dropping out of her grammar after each overruling.
Affirms the teacher identity she claims outright; the 'repeatable craft' framing is flattering rather than revealing.
Precisely captures apology reserved for those who cannot answer, with Malachi's 'it's cool' as the only living reply she accepts.
Directly names the verbatim grievance ledger held alongside the denial of holding onto things; the refrain-repetition evidence is real.
Gets the hoarding of the dangerous assignment plus the two-step where an efficiency reason is offered then immediately supplemented by the real one.
Modest but true discourse pattern — pre-emptive discount followed by exhaustive detail — traceable in four of five openings.
Administers the walkthrough in three stories, receives it in none, and in E5 giving two of them is the stated cost of the birthday; well grounded.
She states the charge refusals and the meetings reason herself; the 'authority without title' gloss adds only a little.
Notices the precise registration of slights but stops at 'declines to pursue', treating her non-confrontation as settled rather than as the ledger substituting for it.
Aggregates her stated self-view (acts when systems fail) with the costs she already narrates; competent summary, little new.
The 'that's just' tic is real and repeated at every point of significance; the coda about colleagues learning not to compliment her is unsupported speculation.
Adds a real nuance to the known confrontation trait: she spends borrowed authority on a specific patient rather than escalating formally.
Directly contradicts her 'I can separate it' claim with a costed leak in every account; obvious once stated but she would not say it.
